name: Fall of Singapore
note: The plan shows the whole operation on the island, 8 to 13 February 1942, not a single field: each block is a brigade, division or corps. The accounts place the formations by sector, not by exact position, so the blocks stand roughly where their sectors lay, and the coastline is only sketched.

phases.title: The island divided into three sectors
phases.text: Two Australian brigades held the west, where the invasion was most likely, III Indian Corps held the north-east and the Southern Area forces the south-east. The Japanese stood across the Johor Strait.
phases.quote: Percival gave Major-General Gordon Bennett's two brigades from the 8th Australian Division responsibility for the western side of Singapore

phases.title: The 5th and 18th Divisions land in the north-west
phases.text: The first wave crossed the strait shortly before 20:30. The main weight, about 13,000 men, fell on the 22nd Australian Brigade, which numbered just 3,000.
phases.quote: The main weight of the Japanese force, about 13,000 men, from 16 assault battalions, with five in reserve, attacked the 22nd Australian Brigade.

phases.title: The 22nd Brigade falls back towards the centre
phases.text: The Australian battalions that had been engaged regrouped and moved back east from the coast, and the Japanese divisions followed inland. The Australians were pushed back further in the early morning.
phases.quote: the three Australian battalions that had been engaged sought to regroup, moving back east from the coast towards the centre of the island, which was completed mainly in good order

phases.title: Indian battalions are sent to the Australians
phases.text: Percival, who expected further landings in the north-east, sent no help until the morning of 9 February. Two half-strength battalions of the 12th Indian Brigade then reached Bennett around noon.
phases.quote: Percival did not reinforce the 22nd Brigade until the morning of 9 February, sending two half-strength battalions from the 12th Indian Infantry Brigade. The Indians reached Bennett around noon.

phases.title: The Imperial Guards attack the 27th Brigade
phases.text: The Guards crossed on the 27th Brigade's front, near the causeway, and some reached the shore. Mortars, machine-guns and burning oil on the water caused them severe casualties, and Yamashita ordered them to press on.
phases.quote: Late on 9 February, the Imperial Guards began assaulting the positions held by the 27th Brigade, concentrating on those held by the 2/26th Battalion.

phases.title: The 27th Brigade withdraws from the causeway
phases.text: Maxwell could not contact the 22nd Brigade and feared encirclement. His brigade withdrew east of the Bukit Timah Road, and the Allies lost the beaches by the causeway. Bennett later said he had not authorised the move.
phases.quote: the 2/26th Battalion was forced to withdraw to a position east of the Bukit Timah Road

phases.title: Guards armour lands at Kranji; 8th Indian Brigade sent
phases.text: The withdrawal opened the Kranji shore, and Guards armoured units landed there unopposed and began ferrying across artillery and armour. Key sent the 8th Indian Brigade from reserve to retake the high ground south of the Causeway.
phases.quote: The opening at Kranji made it possible for Imperial Guards armoured units to land there unopposed, after which they were able to begin ferrying across their artillery and armour.

phases.title: The Jurong Line collapses
phases.text: Taylor misread his orders and withdrew the 22nd Brigade east. The 12th Indian Brigade was then pulled back to the road junction near Bukit Panjang, and the 44th Indian Brigade on the left of the line withdrew in the same way.
phases.quote: Jurong Line eventually collapsed after the 12th Indian Brigade was withdrawn by its commander, Brigadier Archie Paris, to the road junction near Bukit Panjang

phases.title: X Battalion goes forward to Bukit Timah
phases.text: Wavell ordered a counter-attack to retake the Jurong Line. Bennett allocated X Battalion, 200 poorly trained and equipped replacements, and it advanced to an assembly area near Bukit Timah, where it camped to wait.
phases.quote: The battalion, consisting of poorly trained and equipped replacements, advanced to an assembly area near Bukit Timah.

phases.title: The Japanese fall on X Battalion
phases.text: The 5th Division aimed at Bukit Panjang and the 18th Division at Bukit Timah. They fell on X Battalion in its assembly area, and two thirds of it were killed or wounded.
phases.quote: the 5th Division aimed its advance towards Bukit Panjang, while the 18th Division struck out towards Bukit Timah. They fell upon X Battalion, which had camped in its assembly area while waiting to launch its counter-attack, and two-thirds of the battalion was killed or wounded.

phases.title: The Japanese take the Bukit Timah area
phases.text: The Japanese attacked the 22nd Brigade again around the Reformatory Road. Its fighting strength fell to a few hundred men, and the Japanese captured the Bukit Timah area with the garrison's main food and fuel depots.
phases.quote: The fighting strength of the 22nd Brigade—which had borne the brunt of the Japanese attacks—had been reduced to a few hundred men and the Japanese had captured the Bukit Timah area, including the main food and fuel depots of the garrison.

phases.title: The 27th Brigade's counter-attack is repulsed
phases.text: The 27th Brigade was ordered to recapture Bukit Panjang as a first step towards retaking Bukit Timah. The Imperial Guards repulsed it, and the brigade was split in half on either side of the Bukit Timah Road.
phases.quote: the 27th Australian Brigade was later ordered to recapture Bukit Panjang as a preliminary move in retaking Bukit Timah. The counter-attack was repulsed by the Imperial Guards and the 27th Australian Brigade was split in half on either side of the Bukit Timah Road

phases.title: The Commonwealth forces pull back to a city perimeter
phases.text: The Commonwealth forces withdrew from the northern shore and Changi to a perimeter around Singapore City at the eastern end of the island, with harassing attacks all the way. The 44th Brigade held from Buona Vista to Pasir Panjang.
phases.quote: the order was given for a 28 mi (45 km) perimeter to be established around Singapore City at the eastern end of the island
